column3: “Engage in battle on it” is rendered “conquer it.”
“Has stood with Ephraim” is rendered “have camped in Ephraim.”
“Show quietness” is rendered “be calm,” and “stumps of pieces of firewood” as “stubs of … firebrands.”
“Demolish” is rendered “terrorize,” and NASB adds “in its walls.”
NASB puts the second half in parentheses and adds “so that it is no longer.”
The wordplay “believe … be established” is rendered “believe … last,” and NASB adds “surely.”
“Make weary” is rendered “try the patience of.”
“To his knowing” is rendered “at the time He knows enough.”
“The end of the canals” is rendered “the remotest part of the rivers.”
“The River” is rendered “the Euphrates,” and NASB adds “that is”; “hair of the feet” becomes “hair of the legs.”
